why: Each frame the sprite renderer hands each object it draws a place for its tiles in OBJ VRAM (its sprite state's +0x08, u16) from a running count over all it draws before it, and a palette slot (+0x15's high nibble) from the slots taken before it; a frame or palette already loaded this frame is given its place or slot again. The code is the same in both games, but what each draws (MegaMan's own sprite, his flash and sparks, BN6's own effects, a native) differs, so the numbers do. A family object's place and slot are read as their rank among those the family's objects drawn that frame take: the family's own draw order and sharing, compared; what else is drawn among them is no part of the family's. One not drawn (its +0x00 bit 0x02 clear, its sprite's state's +0x03 bit 0x02 clear: the renderer's own test, as an object can hide its sprite alone; or its cache, +0x24, clear: the renderer passed it over, NumberMan's companion while visible) keeps the place it was last drawn at, so it keeps that rank; one whose place moved undrawn is compared as it is; one never drawn has no place the renderer gave it (its sprite state holds its slot's last occupant's, or its set-up's; its spawn clears its record short of them): none, in both. Slot 15 (none taken) stays. The frames the family draws are compared from its sprite's own data (+0x1C, +0x20) and its cache (+0x24), so its tile counts are. The same places of what is not the family's are masked (the renderer's slots, the renderer's palette slot). A family object whose place (or slot) in BN5 is one an object not the family's draws that frame (the renderer keeps a frame or palette already loaded where it is: the Dark Soul's buster's arm and muzzle, 3:0x03 and 3:0x06, the same art as BN5's MegaMan's own, which BN6's MegaMan draws from BN6's) is ranked in neither game, read as shared in both (tools/xdiff_masks.py, SHARED).
evidence: the renderer: BN5 0x081C7F26-0x081C804C and BN6 0x081D64BE-0x081D65E4 (the IWRAM renderer's ROM copies), the same code but for their literal pools

a sprite's state not shown is skipped, its cache cleared and its place kept: BN5 0x081C7F9A-0x081C7FAC / BN6 0x081D6532-0x081D6544 (ldrb [r5,#3]; tst #2); metfire_v1: the fire column's object shown and its sprite not (t199-t203, t317-t321), its place the one it was last given (BN5 29, BN6 59), and a column's place before its first draw its slot's last occupant's (t247: BN5 59, BN6 29)

the tile place: BN5 0x081C7FF4-0x081C7FFC / BN6 0x081D658C-0x081D6594, the running count's value stored and the frame's tiles added to it (BN6 0x081D6562-0x081D6566, 0x081D6590-0x081D6594); a frame already copied this frame is given its place again (found at BN6 0x081D66A8-0x081D66C6, stored at 0x081D65B8); a sprite not drawn keeps its old place, its cache cleared (BN6 0x081D653A-0x081D6544)

the palette slot: BN5 0x081C803A-0x081C8048 / BN6 0x081D65D2-0x081D65E0, the slot's number shifted into +0x15's high nibble, none where it reads 0xF (BN6 0x081D65BE-0x081D65C8); the slot found or taken: BN6 0x081D6640-0x081D666A

in every spec the family's ranks are the same in both games on every frame a family object is drawn in both (cangard_v1: 2084 tile places, 2084 palette slots; cangard_v1_keys: 1813 and 1798), with no family object drawn in one game alone
